Hello all! I'd like to share a story and I was wondering if anybody here has had any experiences with predators or aggressive animals on the trail or in your camp.

Here's my mountain lion story, well, the most exciting of the two... I was going out for a overnight solo trip on the PCT right near Castle Peak which is in the Sierras, near Truckee,CA. I had a good hike in, about 6 miles. I set up camp near the southern shoulder of Castle Peak and had a prime spot with an excellent view. After setting up camp I explored a bit of my surroundings and took some photos. Then I made some dinner and stashed my bear vault. I was just relaxing by my little camp fire for a few hours and decided to call it a night. At this time it was about half past midnight. I queued up a playlist on my phone and as I was putting my ear buds in I looked to my right and what I saw was terrifying!

A mountain lion was standing there about 4 feet away from me! As I reached for my bear spray, which to my benefit was right at my side. As I did so, the mountain lion started taking another step towards me. I ripped off the safety and gave it a blast, point blank. At that very moment a gust of wind swirled the spray into my eyes as well. I was blinded, it was so painful! I just knew I was dead. I had no chance in that fight even if I could see. But I must have gotten the lion pretty good, because after about 10-15 min(unsure of the exact timeline, time ceased to exist the moment I saw it) of splashing water in my eyes I regained some of my vision back and the lion was nowhere within my albeit limited sight.

Needless to say, I didn't sleep a wink that night. I spent the rest of the night grabbing anything within reach to keep my little fire going. About every 5-10 min I would stand up and shine my headlamp out towards the tree line and yell and blast a tiny air horn(which I had inexplicably packed) to further ward it off. There were several times I could see glowing eyes surveying me from the darkness.

When dawns light started to break and I felt I had enough light to pack up and be secure in my vision, I hightailed it out of there. But as I was surveying my camp before leaving I noticed somethings very unnerving. There were mountain lion paw prints surrounding my camp. I swear they weren't there when I arrived. Several different sizes and some that seemed to indicate this one had a cub with it. I snapped a couple pics and hit the trail. I made the return trip in double, maybe triple time, bear (lion) spray in hand!

Mtn. lion paw print with my size 10 boot for scale

Mtn. lion Paw print

Other sizes

So, I'm wondering if any of you has any similar experiences on the trail or in camp?
Has anyone encountered any predators on the trail or in camp?

I had a couple of encounters with wildlife while I was camping/hiking. On a trail at Yellowstone National Park we were hiking to Fairy Meadows. On the way there we encountered two bison on the trial. ON the trail. It felt like a Pokemon adventure except I can die. We just went off trail to get around them and keeping the a good distance from them. Eventually we hit another one. this time getting around it was harder than the last time. Beyond the Bison was a bridge to cross a large creek then onto some planks to cross muddy grounds. Of course we jumped the creek and got across. Another one was last year we came across a bear and it just sat there sleeping. The rattlesnake was encountered on a trail, we just walked around them as well.
While camping we came across a skunk. Good thing they hate being noticed.

Cool, thanks for sharing your experiences! From my limited experience at Yellowstone (Family camping/road trip when I was younger) it seems to be teeming with wildlife. I remember seeing more variety of wildlife in a week in that park than most anyplace else I've been. I've always wanted to go back, I will someday.

All totalled ran across 4 mountain lions over the span of 6 years in Southern AZ and 1 in Southern Nevada. None of the were 'agressive' but one instance I was actively tracked by a pair through a canyon, needless to say it was quite the hike knowing I was the hunted.

One of my very first solo backpacking trips I had a small group of javalinas come tearing through my camp around 230am. Really tore up my sleeping bag after I was able to shimmy out of it and crushed a brand new snow peak 1400 trek set. That was a terrible way to wake up and the smell of their piss all over my stuff took several cleanings to get rid of.

And of course countless encounters with rattlers but none were in a bad mood luckly.

One of the funniest sights ever was seeing a black bear I inadvertently spooked slide down a tree and hit the ground running away. Just seeing this big ball of fur coming down that tree, half controlled decent the other half falling, priceless.

Monster-Classification

Raw DD (RDD) : usually this type of monster relies on one of their skills (usually their 2nd or 3rd skills) as their sources of damage: lushen, katarina, kahli, etc

violent DD (VDD) : this type of monster potential increase with violent rune: camilla, kahli, raoq, guillaume, all chimeras, perna, tyron, etc

speed DD (SDD) : a type of damage dealer that increasing his damage according to aspd : all samurais, theomars, tesharion, hwa, etc

HP-based DD (HPDD) : DD that benefit greatly from his HP: eshir, vigor, beast monks, darion, jubilee

DEF-based DD (DEFDD) : DD that benefit greatly from his DEF : groggo, velajuel, dark archangel

SS - Support that want to Recycle their skills fast or support that benefit greatly from speed : chasun, veromos, eladriel, briand, shannon

Speed Demons (SD) - monster that you want to be the fastest one no matter what : megan, bernard, chloe, verde

Crowd-Control (CC) : Debuffer team: tyron, barreta, aria, thrain, etc

Bomber (BOMB) : water wind light kobold, and fire dark joker
